records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14
records.source: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.translation: De två robusta konstanter är *inte* utbytbara och modulen vägrar att låtsas att de är. 1,4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) är ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, faktorn som gör MAD för ett normalt urval till en opartisk uppskattning av dess SD. Ett glidande intervall är ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, det absoluta värdet av en *difference* av två observationer, så dess skala är ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` och dess median är ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplicera en median rörlig räckvidd med 1.4826 överskattar sigma med exakt ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% bredare gränser, vilket är skillnaden mellan att fånga en drift och inte. Båda konstanterna beräknas från ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` här av samma anledning som c4 beräknades från gammafunktionen.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#5
records.source: 1. **It is rank-based**, so it is invariant under any monotone transform of the feature. Half a spaCR measurement table is log-normal-ish — areas, integrated intensities, ratios spanning three orders of magnitude — and whether ``cell_area`` or ``log(cell_area)`` was measured must not change which feature comes top. It does change Cohen's d. 2. **It assumes nothing about the distributions**: not normality, not equal variance, not even symmetry. The alternatives assume at least one of those, and a segmented-object feature satisfies none of them. 3. **It is bounded and unit-free**, so four hundred features measured in px², in counts and in dimensionless ratios are comparable on one axis. That is what ranking *requires*, and it is exactly why an effect size in the feature's own units cannot do the job.
records.context: 1. **It is rank-based**, so it is invariant under any monotone transform of the feature. Half a spaCR measurement table is log-normal-ish — areas, integrated intensities, ratios spanning three orders of magnitude — and whether ``cell_area`` or ``log(cell_area)`` was measured must not change which feature comes top. It does change Cohen's d. 2. **It assumes nothing about the distributions**: not normality, not equal variance, not even symmetry. The alternatives assume at least one of those, and a segmented-object feature satisfies none of them. 3. **It is bounded and unit-free**, so four hundred features measured in px², in counts and in dimensionless ratios are comparable on one axis. That is what ranking *requires*, and it is exactly why an effect size in the feature's own units cannot do the job.
records.translation: 1. **Det är rangbaserat**, så resultatet är oförändrat vid varje monoton transformation av egenskapen. Hälften av kolumnerna i en spaCR-mättabell är ungefär lognormalfördelade — areor, integrerade intensiteter och kvoter över tre storleksordningar — och om ``cell_area`` eller ``log(cell_area)`` mäts får inte ändra vilken egenskap som hamnar överst. Det ändrar Cohens d. 2. **Det gör inga antaganden om fördelningarna**: inte normalitet, lika varians eller ens symmetri. Alternativen antar minst en av dessa egenskaper, och en egenskap hos ett segmenterat objekt uppfyller ingen av dem. 3. **Det är begränsat och enhetslöst**, så fyrahundra egenskaper mätta i px², antal och dimensionslösa kvoter kan jämföras på samma axel. Det är vad rangordning *kräver*, och precis därför kan en effektstorlek i egenskapens egen enhet inte användas.

records.source: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. A preview that printed "velocity 4.2" while the user was thinking in µm/s would be worse than printing nothing, so the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of quietly borrowing the 1.78 px/µm default.

En förhandsgranskning som skrev ut "velocity 4.2" medan användaren tänkte i µm/s skulle vara värre än att skriva ut ingenting, så att kalibreringsfälten börjar med **inte angivna**, varje hastighet bär sin enhet, och medan kalibreringen är okänd säger panelen det i ord istället för att tyst låna 1,78 px / µm-standarden.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#7
records.source: **The 1.4826.** For a Gaussian, ``MAD = Phi^-1(0.75) * sigma = 0.6745 * sigma``, so ``sigma = MAD / 0.6745 = 1.4826 * MAD``. Multiplying by :data:`MAD_TO_SIGMA` makes the MAD a *consistent estimator of sigma* under normality, which is what lets the threshold be read on the familiar scale — "3.5 SD" — while never being computed from an SD that the outliers could inflate. The constant is the whole reason ``k`` is comparable to a z-score cut-off at all; without it, ``k`` would be in units of "MADs" and 3.5 would mean something different for every column.
records.context: **The 1.4826.** For a Gaussian, ``MAD = Phi^-1(0.75) * sigma = 0.6745 * sigma``, so ``sigma = MAD / 0.6745 = 1.4826 * MAD``. Multiplying by :data:`MAD_TO_SIGMA` makes the MAD a *consistent estimator of sigma* under normality, which is what lets the threshold be read on the familiar scale — "3.5 SD" — while never being computed from an SD that the outliers could inflate. The constant is the whole reason ``k`` is comparable to a z-score cut-off at all; without it, ``k`` would be in units of "MADs" and 3.5 would mean something different for every column.
records.translation: **Den 1.4826.** För en Gaussisk, ``MAD = Phi^-1(0.75) * sigma = 0.6745 * sigma``, så ``sigma = MAD / 0.6745 = 1.4826 * MAD``. Multiplikation med :data:`MAD_TO_SIGMA` gör MAD till en *konsistent skattning av sigma* vid normalfördelning, vilket gör att tröskelvärdet kan läsas på den välbekanta skalan – "3,5 SD" – samtidigt som det aldrig beräknas från en SD som avvikande värden kan blåsa upp. Konstanten är hela anledningen till att ``k`` är jämförbart med en z-poängsgräns alls; utan det, skulle ``k`` vara i enheter av "MADs" och 3,5 skulle betyda något annat för varje kolumn.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion#3
records.source: ``distinct_values`` runs one ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` per ``(database, table)`` pair the chosen column appears in — and the columns a user actually excludes on (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) hold a handful of distinct values across the whole table, so the LIMIT is never reached and SQLite scans every row. Measured on a 200 000-row × 8-table measurements.db with a warm page cache: **196 ms per column**, and the column combo is editable, so ``currentTextChanged`` fires on every keystroke. Eight quick edits froze the window for **894 ms** in one unbroken block; ``set_source`` itself cost 183 ms and a single deliberate column choice 220 ms. Threaded, the same three are 29 ms, 5 ms and 2 ms.
records.context: ``distinct_values`` runs one ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` per ``(database, table)`` pair the chosen column appears in — and the columns a user actually excludes on (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) hold a handful of distinct values across the whole table, so the LIMIT is never reached and SQLite scans every row. Measured on a 200 000-row × 8-table measurements.db with a warm page cache: **196 ms per column**, and the column combo is editable, so ``currentTextChanged`` fires on every keystroke. Eight quick edits froze the window for **894 ms** in one unbroken block; ``set_source`` itself cost 183 ms and a single deliberate column choice 220 ms. With worker execution, the same three are 29 ms, 5 ms and 2 ms.
records.translation: ``distinct_values`` kör en ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` för varje par ``(database, table)`` där den valda kolumnen förekommer — och kolumnerna som en användare faktiskt utesluter efter (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) innehåller bara ett fåtal distinkta värden i hela tabellen, så LIMIT nås aldrig och SQLite läser varje rad. Mätt på en measurements.db med 200 000 rader × 8 tabeller och varm sidcache: **196 ms per kolumn**. Kolumnkombinationsrutan är redigerbar, så ``currentTextChanged`` utlöses vid varje tangenttryckning. Åtta snabba redigeringar frös fönstret i **894 ms** i ett obrutet block; ``set_source`` kostade 183 ms och ett enskilt avsiktligt kolumnval 220 ms. Med trådad körning tar samma tre operationer 29 ms, 5 ms och 2 ms.

records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** A run used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the run that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** A processing session used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the processing session that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.translation: **Ett behandlingssessions-id, på varje loggrad och varje utdata.** En behandlingssession brukade vara ospårbar. Loggen sa att ett fält misslyckades; registret sa att en artefakt fanns; ingenting kopplade ihop dem, så "visa mig allt från bearbetningssessionen som producerade den här filen" hade inget svar. :func:`run_context` präglar ett id, stämplar det på varje :class:`logging.LogRecord` som skapas någonstans i processen, skriver en JSONL-logg per bearbetningssession som :func:`read_run_log` läser tillbaka och överlämnar *samma*-id till :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. En logglinje och en utgång kan därför sammanfogas på ``run_id``, vilket är hela poängen.

records.label: spacr.seg_qc#9
records.source: ``over-segmentation`` (shattered objects) Two signatures. Absolutely: at least ``seg_qc_tiny_fraction`` (0.30) of the field's objects are under ``seg_qc_min_diameter`` (5 px) across — spaCR's diameter estimator already discards components below 4 px as debris, and nothing 5 px across survives a crop-and-measure as an object. Relative to the plate: the field holds ``seg_qc_size_ratio``-fold more objects than the plate median at ``1/seg_qc_size_ratio`` of its median diameter. That knob defaults to 1.4 = sqrt(2) on purpose — two objects welded into one have sqrt(2) times the equivalent diameter of one, and one object split in two has 1/sqrt(2) of it, so 1.4 is the fused-pair / split-in-half signature itself rather than an arbitrary tolerance.
records.context: ``over-segmentation`` (shattered objects) Two signatures. Absolutely: at least ``seg_qc_tiny_fraction`` (0.30) of the microscope field of view's objects are under ``seg_qc_min_diameter`` (5 px) across — spaCR's diameter estimator already discards components below 4 px as debris, and nothing 5 px across survives an image-region extraction-and-measurement operation as an object. Relative to the laboratory microplate: the microscope field of view holds ``seg_qc_size_ratio``-fold more objects than the laboratory microplate median at ``1/seg_qc_size_ratio`` of its median diameter. That knob defaults to 1.4 = sqrt(2) on purpose — two objects welded into one have sqrt(2) times the equivalent diameter of one, and one object split in two has 1/sqrt(2) of it, so 1.4 is the fused-pair / split-in-half signature itself rather than an arbitrary tolerance.
records.translation: ``over-segmentation`` (splittrade objekt) Två kännetecken. Absolut: minst ``seg_qc_tiny_fraction`` (0.30) av fältets objekt är smalare än ``seg_qc_min_diameter`` (5 px) — spaCR:s diameteruppskattare förkastar redan komponenter som är mindre än 4 px som skräp, och inget som är 5 px brett överlever en utskärnings- och mätningsoperation som ett objekt. Relativt plattan: fältet innehåller ``seg_qc_size_ratio`` gånger fler objekt än plattans median vid ``1/seg_qc_size_ratio`` av dess mediandiameter. Parametern är avsiktligt 1.4 = sqrt(2) som standard — två objekt som svetsas samman har sqrt(2) gånger diametern hos ett objekt, och ett objekt som delas i två får 1/sqrt(2) av diametern, så 1.4 är själva kännetecknet för ett sammanfogat par eller en halvering, inte en godtycklig tolerans.

records.source: **A request** (:class:`ObjectRequest`) is neither: it is one act of routing. "Open exactly these twelve objects, because they are the cells this model called infected and the annotator called uninfected." A filter and a selection are *state* that every view reads; a request is an *event* that travels once, from the view that made it to the view that can show it. It carries the reason with it, because a view showing twelve crops out of ninety thousand has to be able to say why those twelve — otherwise they read as the whole dataset.

records.source: **Backward compatibility is the whole difficulty.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and INVARIANTS §6 is the trap: a key *absent* from the dict means the pipeline falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a run from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.context: **Backward compatibility is the whole difficulty.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and INVARIANTS §6 is the trap: a structured-data name *absent* from the key-value mapping means the workflow falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a processing session from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.translation: **Bakåtkompatibilitet är hela svårigheten.** En inställning CSV skriven innan detta finns i varje användares projektmapp, och INVARIANTS §6 är fällan: ett strukturerat datanamn *saknas* från nyckel-värde-mappningen innebär att arbetsflödet faller tillbaka till sin egen standard, som kan skilja sig från GUI:orna, och ingenting säger det. Varje byte av namn här är därför ett alias, inte en ersättning – :func:`normalize_settings` översätter det gamla namnet och den gamla *underförstådda*-basen till den nya explicita, och en bearbetningssession från en gammal CSV gör exakt vad den gjorde tidigare.

records.label: spacr.utils.console_safe#1
records.source: Console decoration must never be able to end a run. No Windows codepage encodes spaCR's own output set -- ``▸`` (U+25B8) is absent from cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *and* cp936, and the box-drawing frame is absent from cp1252 -- and neither does any of them encode the domain vocabulary that ends up in settings values, such as the parental strain ``Δku80`` or a ``µm`` voxel size. Printing either to a non-UTF-8 stream raises ``UnicodeEncodeError``, and on Windows that is the normal case the moment stdout is redirected: a batch-queue job, ``spacr-run``, a legacy console.
records.context: Console decoration must never terminate a run. Windows code pages do not encode every spaCR output character. For example, ``▸`` is missing from cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *and* cp936, and cp1252 lacks the frame characters. Settings may also contain ``Δku80`` or ``µm``. Writing these values to a non-UTF-8 stream raises ``UnicodeEncodeError``. On Windows, this commonly occurs when stdout is redirected by a batch job, ``spacr-run``, or a legacy console.
records.translation: Konsoldekoration får aldrig avsluta en körning. Ingen Windows-kodsida kan koda spaCR:s egen utdatauppsättning — ``▸`` (U+25B8) saknas i cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *och* cp936, och cp1252 saknar även ramtecknen — och ingen av dem kan heller koda domänord som förekommer i inställningsvärden, exempelvis moderstammen ``Δku80`` eller en voxelstorlek i ``µm``. Att skriva något av detta till en ström som inte är UTF-8 utlöser ``UnicodeEncodeError``. I Windows är detta normalt så snart stdout omdirigeras: ett jobb i en batchkö, ``spacr-run`` eller en äldre konsol.
